title: The bus speaks TCP between boxes and on Windows
intention: The bus carries messages over TCP between boxes and on Windows, while staying on Unix sockets inside a Linux box, so a device on akiendell can reach a bus and the buses on two boxes can reach each other.
why: Python on Windows has no socket.AF_UNIX (measured 2026-11-04 on akiendell: the web server died at cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py:95), so no device on a Windows box can reach any bus; and buses on two boxes (outline 5.4.2.8.1) can only reach each other over the network. Akien 2026-11-04: 'yes please' (outline 5.4.2.11.4).
traces_to: Outline 5.4.2.8 (one bus per cairn instance, extended across hosts), 5.4.2.8.1 (a bus per box, the buses talk) and 5.4.2.11.4 (TCP between boxes and on Windows); Telos: running multiple heavy tasks at once across Akien's boxes; Law 3 (the transport choice is settled by measuring, 5.4.2.11).
how: Give the bus an address that is either a Unix socket path or host:port. server.py:523 also listens on TCP beside bus.sock: 127.0.0.1 plain on Windows (no AF_UNIX there), and on the home box the LAN, TLS only; remote.py exchange() picks the transport from the address (AF_UNIX where it exists and the bus is on this box, TCP otherwise). Same wire format (one JSON request, one JSON reply), so callers do not change. Box to box is TLS in the bus itself (open-06cfefbe745e, Akien 2026-11-04: 'TLS sounds like the win to me, more in line with no extra things to set up'; replaces the ssh answer): stdlib ssl over the same TCP socket; each box has its own key + self-signed certificate under ~/.cairn (made by cairn install, beside the cairn-home question); each side pins the other's SHA-256 certificate fingerprint from a list of known boxes and refuses any other; mutual, so both ends are checked. No tunnel, no token, no extra process. Measure TCP loopback latency against the 50 us Unix socket number (5.4.2.11.1). BUILDER BRIEF: A Haiku builder needs: (1) the files: cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/server.py (listener at :523), cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/__main__.py:23, cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py (exchange at :87-104, _spawn :147, _setsid :197); (2) the port: env CAIRN_BUS_TCP_PORT, default 7419 (unassigned by IANA), checked free at build; (3) the selection rule above, verbatim; (4) that the wire format must not change; (5) the Windows spawn flags DETACHED_PROCESS|CREATE_NO_WINDOW as in launchers/superclaude _sc_spawn_detached; (6) the gate is mutual TLS with pinned fingerprints (open-06cfefbe745e); a box whose CAIRN_HOME_HOST is another box dials that host's bus over TLS; the fingerprint exchange is a cairn install step; (7) proofs in cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/ and cairn/tools/bus_client/proofs/, a tooth that forces the TCP path on Linux (AF_UNIX hidden) so it is provable here; (8) the latency bench is scratch today (5.4.2.11.1), so record numbers in the ticket, not a new tool.
falsifier: Done when (a) on akiendell, a fresh python using cairn.tools.bus_client.remote.RemoteBus().list() gets an answer from a bus it lazily started, over TCP 127.0.0.1, no AF_UNIX error; (b) from akiendell a request reaches the bus on akiendelllinux over TLS with both fingerprints pinned, and a caller or a server whose certificate fingerprint is not on the list is refused, and the bus's LAN port refuses plain TCP; (c) on Linux the Unix-socket p50 round trip stays within 10% of the 50 us measured at outline 5.4.2.11.1, and TCP loopback is measured and recorded. Horizon: the first box-to-box message. Wrong intent if pinned TLS adds a setup step a new box cannot do inside cairn install.
decisions: Unix sockets stay the transport inside a Linux box; TCP is added only where Unix cannot go (Windows, box to box).
The wire format (one JSON request, one JSON reply) does not change; callers do not change.
remote.py picks AF_UNIX when socket has it and the bus is on this box, else TCP.

Box to box is mutual TLS with pinned certificate fingerprints, in the bus itself; the home's LAN port speaks TLS only; on Windows the local bus listens on 127.0.0.1 (open-06cfefbe745e, Akien 2026-11-04).
remote.py spawns the bus on Windows with DETACHED_PROCESS|CREATE_NO_WINDOW, as launchers/superclaude _sc_spawn_detached does.
A proof tooth forces the TCP path on Linux (AF_UNIX hidden) so the Windows path is provable on this box.
Bus-to-bus routing by name is out of scope: a follow-on ticket.
